subject: Archaeology
title: The Lost Labyrinth of Hawara
description: A quick win: understand The Lost Labyrinth of Hawara.

hook.text: Ancient Greek writers described an Egyptian building more impressive than the pyramids. Then it vanished.

buildup.text: Herodotus visited the Labyrinth at Hawara and wrote that it had 3,000 rooms on two levels.

discovery.text: Flinders Petrie excavated the site in 1888 and found only a field of limestone chips — the building was gone.

twist.text: Romans quarried the entire structure for building material. They recycled one wonder to build another.

climax.text: Ground-penetrating radar in 2008 detected massive foundations underground, confirming something huge was there.

punchline.text: The building the Greeks called the greatest ever made was recycled into Roman.

quiz.question: What happened to the legendary Labyrinth at Hawara?
options: It was buried by a sandstorm and remains intact underground
Romans quarried the entire structure for building material
An earthquake collapsed it into the Nile floodplain

details.summary: Ancient Greek writers described a vast labyrinth near Hawara that surpassed even the pyramids in grandeur. Modern excavations have found remains of an enormous mortuary temple of Amenemhat III, but most of the structure was quarried away centuries ago for building stone.
details.whyItMatters: The lost labyrinth illustrates how ancient accounts can guide modern archaeology while also showing that some of the ancient world's greatest structures have been completely destroyed beyond recovery.
takeaways: Greek writers described it as more impressive than the pyramids
Built as Amenemhat III's mortuary temple at Hawara
Most of the structure was quarried away for building stone

faq.question: What did ancient writers say about the labyrinth?
faq.answer: Herodotus visited and described a complex of 3,000 rooms on two levels — half above ground, half below — with courts, passages, and halls that amazed him more than the pyramids. Strabo and Pliny also described its enormous scale and complexity.

faq.question: What has modern archaeology found at the site?
faq.answer: Ground-penetrating radar and excavations have revealed foundations of an enormous structure consistent with ancient descriptions. However, Roman and later builders quarried the stone for centuries, leaving only foundations and scattered fragments of what was once there.
